prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from acceptance (bag-drop/transfer induction) through screening, sorting, make-up, to outbound load control handoff. Elements: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (records/stages accepted bag without changing flight; sends Oversize Exception Ticket, used by Image Resolution Desk to confirm make-up position); Bag Tag Printer (unique-ID tag; Calibration Witness Tag; replacement tag only after authorized confirmation); Transfer Bag Feeder (meters transfer bags, no check bypass; sends Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station); Induction Tray Conveyor (spacing/metering; priority admission after scan); Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (tag-flight association; routing; screening profile; sort plan; alternate routes; exceptions to Secondary Inspection Chute; cutoff profiles; receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; records screening disposition/release state per flight); Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (induction permissive; Recovery Route Card; capacity matching; assigns bags to active make-up lanes); Flight Data Gateway, alias Lantern (flight identity/timing, revisions, dispatch targets, connection windows; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory); Primary Crossbelt Sorter, alias Juniper (Chute Occupancy Note; routes by destination, status, cutoff priority); North Gate Scanner, alias Kestrel, and South Gate Scanner (Manual Rescan Receipt; outcomes; verify readable ID); Image Resolution Desk; Secondary Inspection Chute (retains until disposition); Bag Reconciliation Station (Bag Match Query); East/West Make-Up Conveyor (controlled delivery); Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit, alias Orchard (bag order/position; receives Carousel Release Slip after position/flight check); Outbound Load Control Desk (reconciles build vs permitted load before closeout). Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor, alias Tern (congestion, recovery, priorities, deferral; authorizes make-up release only within processing window; coordinates with airline ground ops); Explosives Response Team, alias Pebble (Custody Seal Log); Security Duty Manager (resolves security release holds); Maintenance Technician (reports equipment restrictions); Airline Ramp Coordinator (sends Carousel Release Slip; confirms staffing/equipment/sequence before accepting build). States: clear, exception, awaiting review; manual resolution when image/identity exception blocks automatic disposition. Requirements: hold missing/conflicting/oversized; induction needs valid record/route/equipment; interlocks stop feed; incomplete exam never clear; awaiting-review/screening barred from make-up; threat suspends routing; cutoffs include allowances;

New part:
S156: Image Resolution Desk presents the available bag image and exception details to the operator for review.
S157: The operator compares visible bag features with the recorded tag number and the handling data associated with the bag.
S158: The operator confirms that the image is legible enough to support a decision and does not rely on an uncertain visual match.
S159: Image Resolution Desk uses the rescan receipt to confirm that a second image was captured under the approved procedure.
S160: When the image remains inconclusive, the operator requests a physical inspection through the established inspection process.
S161: The identity check verifies that the physical tag is attached to the inspected bag and that its number agrees with the recorded bag identity.
S162: Baggage Control System checks the recorded bag identity against the current routing data before any disposition is committed.
S163: Flight Data Gateway provides the flight data used to validate the bag's assigned destination and service date.
S164: Bag Reconciliation Station records whether the inspected bag matches the expected flight assignment.
S165: A mismatch places the bag on hold until an authorized operator resolves the discrepancy or escalates it.
S166: Juniper holds the affected bag from automatic sorting while the manual disposition remains unresolved.
S167: Kestrel captures a readable tag image when the bag is presented for a permitted scan.
S168: North Gate Scanner records the tag read and image data needed to support an operator's identity check.
S169: Secondary Inspection Chute provides a controlled location for bags requiring physical examination.
S170: Explosives Response Team conducts any security examination assigned under applicable procedures.
S171: Baggage Operations Supervisor approves the operational disposition when the case exceeds the operator's authority.
S172: After the identity and flight checks pass, Baggage Control System authorizes the bag to rejoin its previously assigned screening and sort path.
S173: Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the bag remains eligible for inclusion in the planned flight load.
S174: Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms any flight-side constraint that could prevent the reconciled bag from being accepted.
S175: Concourse Zone Controller applies the authorized routing state without bypassing required screening controls.
S176: Maintenance Technician uses the witness tag to verify that the applicable calibration status was witnessed before equipment returns to service.
S177: If a route or flight assignment has changed, the operator obtains approval before the bag is released into the revised process.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
